title: The potato storage gamble
summary: Agra potatoes: ₹1,185 in March 2020, ₹2,505 in October. Break-even storage budget: ₹1,062 per quintal.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the yearly harvest-to-autumn storage question at Agra, with 6 earlier seasons to learn from.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of Agra daily modal prices (≥8 reports)
caveats: No cold-storage rent is cited, so no net profit is claimed.
Stored and fresh potatoes may differ in grade.

scenes.headline: March 2020
scenes.caption: Potatoes are harvested in early spring and often held in cold stores in western Uttar Pradesh, which the RBI paper calls the potato belt's key selling point.

scenes.headline: Harvest price
scenes.caption: Agra's March 2020 median: ₹1,185 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The informed bet
scenes.caption: Using only the 6 earlier years, March→October had averaged +₹278. A rule-following trader would store.

scenes.headline: October 2020
scenes.caption: October median: ₹2,505, a change of +111.4%.

scenes.headline: Shrinkage and interest
scenes.caption: Allowing 7% loss and 12% a year interest for 7 months leaves a storage budget of ₹1,062 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹1,062 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

assumptions.value: not in cited evidence; shown as break-even budget

conclusion: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹1,062 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.
